competitorFacts.text: ARC Prize named Tufa Labs and its Duck agent the first-place open-source solution for the June 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 1 prize.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — Duck Harness technical overview
competitorFacts.text: Tufa Labs says its public Duck harness lets an LLM inspect game grids as image and text, write Python in a REPL, and keep context short by evicting older messages. This describes the published Milestone 1 system, not an unverified current submission.
Tufa Labs lists Dries Smit, Isaiah Pressman and Jeroen Cottaar among its AI researchers, with research interests spanning reinforcement learning, self-play and Bayesian methods.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — October 9 public competition post
competitorFacts.text: On October 9, 2026, Tufa Labs described a temporary setback in a public X post and said it remained dedicated to crushing competitors with overwhelming resources and compute.
Yi-Chia Chen’s Kaggle profile lists her as a Competitions Master and a double-degree student at National Taiwan University and Waseda University.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Yi-Chia Chen — Eedi third-place solution write-up
competitorFacts.text: Yi-Chia Chen authored a Kaggle write-up for a third-place solution in Eedi — Mining Misconceptions in Mathematics.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Yi-Chia Chen — public Kaggle profile and avatar
competitorFacts.text: Yi-Chia Chen’s public Kaggle account is threerabbits. The profile lists she/her pronouns and displays an avatar of two rabbits.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Artificial Agency Lab — research and ARC-AGI-3 project
competitorFacts.text: Artificial Agency Lab says it built an ARC-AGI-3 agent combining structured grids and image observations with persistent context updates, keeping model weights fixed; it reports an eighth-place June milestone result.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize places Argon behind Astra’s 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. It reports 62% fewer actions than the human baseline on the 25 public games, matching or beating three speedrun records and coming within 10% on six others.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keep the public-demo action comparison separate from the semi-private Verified score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says API issues prevented complete standard-harness testing: low reasoning completed 42/55 games for 49.8%; medium completed 46/55 for 46.3%; high completed 19/55 and no score was published. Reported scores retain partial credit across all 55 games. Provider adapter preserves opaque reasoning and permits automatic compaction; standard harness carries notes between turns. Costs use introductory $2 input/$10 output per million tokens.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Material limit on harness comparisons. Do not present incomplete standard-harness runs as a clean capability ceiling.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Gemini 4 Argon Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 97.5% at $4.8K with the provider adapter and 49.8% at $5.8K with the standard harness; ARC-AGI-2 91.3% at $0.32/task and ARC-AGI-1 98.5% at $0.16/task. It calls Google DeepMind the second frontier lab above 95% on ARC-AGI-3.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Consequential organizer result. Separate from Kaggle standings. Standard-harness API incompletion is essential context; primary results introduction says 91.2% on v2 while its table and announcement say 91.3%.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize’s October 13 announcement reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at about 3% with its provider adapter and below 1% with the standard harness. The original linked verified-results table, refreshed October 14, gives a matched Low-reasoning comparison of 3.26% versus 0.35%; its headline best configurations differ in reasoning level. Organizer model evaluation, separate from Kaggle team submissions.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Public original read without sign-in in the in-app browser; linked primary results table independently read. Organizer evaluation, separate from Kaggle team standings.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Tufa Labs reclaimed first on the ARC-AGI-3 public Kaggle board with roughly 69%, up from roughly 56%. This is the author’s dated October 13 observation; refresh standings before publication.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer confirmation of a consequential team result already covered in the newspaper’s morning/afternoon reporting; no methods disclosed.

socialPosts.author: OCEANVIN10
socialPosts.summary: OCEAN highlighted the Memento 3 preprint. Its authors report that a fixed language model revises an external rulebook and executable world model; on the 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, they report clearing every level with fewer actions than the human baseline. These are author-reported results on the public set.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A new ARC-AGI-3 research lead for the edition desk. The paper provides a concrete mechanism and results, but the public tutorial set cannot establish private-game performance.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced Yi-Chia Chen at 59.17% on the 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Kaggle board, taking the lead over Tufa Labs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Historical October 9 standings announcement, newly inventoried as a Chollet repost; not a fresh score move. Original and visible context re-read; existing independently verified public visibility preserved.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop argues experiment ideation is the current bottleneck in recursive self-improvement. He claims coding and execution are largely automated, distinguishes reproducing known results from asking novel questions, and says domain-specific improvement recipes still need human-AI collaboration to spread across domains without further generalization breakthroughs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Useful organizer perspective on open-ended evaluation and ARC-AGI. His automation percentages and 12-month scenario are attributed claims, not independently verified results.

socialPosts.author: fchollet
socialPosts.summary: Chollet says Argon has a similar ARC-AGI-3 performance profile to Astra and calls Google back at the frontier, quoting ARC Prize’s result.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Attributed organizer reaction to the Verified release; not a separate evaluation.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop calls Argon the second model family effectively to max out ARC-AGI-3 with a provider adapter and notes a similar backwards bend in action efficiency.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Attributed reaction; preserve the provider-adapter qualification and avoid equating it with Kaggle performance.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize links the Verified leaderboard, reproducible public benchmark code, testing policy and full Gemini 4 Argon results.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Primary evidence links for edition follow-up; no new Kaggle ranking.

socialPosts.author: mhmazur
socialPosts.summary: Replying to Vlad Garbuz’s question about the provider checkpoint used for the DeepSeek evaluation, Mazur says Baseten serves the original DeepSeek V4.1 Flash checkpoint, which natively uses fp8 with mxfp4 experts, without additional quantization. Original reply and parent chain read in regular public-post UI, with no Subscribers restriction. This is Mazur’s testing clarification, not an independently reproduced provider comparison.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New organizer detail for interpreting the October 13 verified DeepSeek evaluation. Keep the native mixed precision distinct from additional provider quantization; no new Kaggle score or ruling.

image.caption: AI-generated editorial illustration. Score panel: Oct 15, 2026 · 1:18 PM EDT; provisional public standings. Characters and props are metaphors.

sections.heading: Special afternoon edition · Google joins the leading model tier
sections.text: Google DeepMind has become the second frontier lab to score above 95% on ARC-AGI-3 in ARC Prize Verified testing. ARC Prize announced 97.5% for Gemini 4 Argon using the provider adapter harness, at a reported evaluation cost of $4,800. Its standard-harness result was 49.8% at $5,800, with API failures preventing a complete run. The announcement also reports 91.3% on ARC-AGI-2 and 98.5% on ARC-AGI-1. These are Verified model evaluations, separate from the Kaggle competition standings.

sections.heading: The harness gap needs its footnote
sections.text: The provider adapter preserves the model’s opaque reasoning state and supports compaction; the standard harness carries forward notes chosen by the model. At low reasoning, the standard-harness evaluation completed 42 of 55 games; medium reasoning completed 46 and scored 46.3%. High reasoning completed only 19, so ARC Prize published no score for it. The reported scores still include all 55 games, retaining partial credit from incomplete runs. That makes the gap important, but it does not isolate a clean estimate of the harness effect. The results page’s introduction says 91.2% for ARC-AGI-2, while its table and the announcement say 91.3%; the latter is the figure attributed above.

sections.heading: Third on Kaggle, with an exclusive team statement
sections.text:
On the separate ARC-AGI-3 Kaggle public board, Son & Mark & Ronen has jumped from seventh to third after improving from 41.97 to 47.25. The five-point advance puts the team ahead of mtg, now fourth on 45.00, and NVARC3, fifth on 43.94. Kaggle’s live roster lists Mark Barney, Son Pham and Ronen Dunlea. The jump was first observed by the collector at 11:47 am Eastern and remains in the latest collected board, dated 1:18 pm. This is a place on the provisional public leaderboard; the private final standings decide the competition.

In an exclusive team statement supplied to The ARC Daily Digest by Mark Barney, the team offered a cryptic description: “We're using the turducken harness, which is the original duck but it's also inside of a chicken that's inside of a turkey.” The statement added: “Shoutouts to Tufa, Daniel Franzen, and NVIDIA for open-sourcing their previous work and leading the way.”

sections.heading: Two citadels still command the heights
sections.text: Tufa Labs remains first on 68.91 and Yi-Chia Chen second on 67.49. Their scores are unchanged from the previous close, and the new third-place team still trails Chen by about twenty points. Below NVARC3, the last dance holds sixth on 43.64. Third place changes the order of the chase without erasing the leaders’ separation. The new illustration sends Son and Mark airborne on a graphics-card chicken toward those two forts: a playful picture of the climb, not a claim about anyone’s real equipment, methods or spending. Ronen is part of the team result and is not depicted.

sections.heading: The organizers’ verdict
sections.text: François Chollet says Argon has a similar ARC-AGI-3 performance profile to Astra and describes Google as back at the frontier. Mike Knoop calls it the second model family effectively to max out ARC-AGI-3 with a provider adapter, while noting the same backwards bend in action efficiency. ARC Prize separately reports that Argon used 62% fewer actions than the human baseline across the 25 public demo games. That action-efficiency comparison is distinct from the 55-game semi-private evaluation and from today’s Kaggle team scores.
